rationale: No supported optimization is clearly applicable to this workflow. The workflow already implements stale-run cancellation via `concurrency.cancel-in-progress: true` (covering P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE), so adding it would be redundant. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST is moot because the build matrix contains only a single OS (`ubuntu_22.04`); with one matrix cell there are no remaining jobs to cancel, and changing `fail-fast` would not preserve or improve coverage. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT is not supported because the precondition of representative successful-duration history is not met: the recent CI history shows only failed runs, so a safe timeout budget cannot be derived. Bazel parallelism/incremental-cache patterns do not apply because the build uses CMake inside Docker, not Bazel. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE offers only modest, observational benefit and its preconditions (measurable repeated dependency fetching, cache inputs including lockfile/environment) are not established for this Docker-based superbuild; caching build outputs is also discouraged by the pattern in favor of dependency state. Adding a cache or timeout without measured history risks weakening required checks or introducing uncaptured failures, so the intended build and test coverage is best preserved unchanged.
